record.why: A refusal that could not say why is not a refusal. Written 2026-09-03 (lane C) from what this record already contains: 5 offers from 5 vendors (ALLNET China, Arace Tech, Evelta (IN), ThinkRobotics (IN), ameriDroid (US)) are here, 5 of them `confidence: verified`, all retrieved 2026-09-02, so it is not that no supplier was found — it is that (a) FOUR OF THE FIVE HAD NOTHING TO SELL on the day they were read — ALLNET China 'Sold out' on every 1 GB and every 2/4 GB-with-eMMC variant (only '2 GB / no eMMC, header' at $55.99 in stock), ameriDroid (US) "'Out of Stock!'; all variants sold out or unavailable", Arace Tech "every combination 'Sold Out'", ThinkRobotics (IN) 'Out of stock' across all 16 variants; only Evelta (IN) reads 'in stock', at INR 2995 — one live source, in one country, is not two — and (b) THE SKU CANNOT BE MATCHED TO THE ROBOT: the Microduck store listing says 1 GB RAM + 32 GB storage and Radxa's own SKU table (RAD-DOC-0084 Rev 1.10 §7 p.8) has no 1 GB + 32 GB eMMC row — 32 GB eMMC pairs only with 4 GB DRAM. So no offer here can be said to be an offer for the part actually fitted, and the unit prices span USD 20.00 (Arace) to USD 41.95 (ameriDroid) across vendors and USD 18 to USD 51.99 across ALLNET's variants alone, so which number a BOM should carry is not decidable either. WHAT SETTLES IT: `cat /proc/meminfo | head -1` and `lsblk` on a production robot (ELECTRONICS-DATASHEET.html §13 row E8), then a re-quote against the SKU that comes back. Lane E owns this file; this `why` states only what the record's own offers and the folder's electrical.host.json identity_vs_fitted already say.
